slide_title: Breathing & Transport of Gases: One-Way Ventilation in Birds
original_text: Breathing and Transport of Gases Ventilation Birds use a one-way ventilation mechanism in lungs nAir flows from trachea to posterior sacs, then into the lung, then into anterior sacs, and is then expelled nFresh air never mixes with used air nIncreases gas-exchange efficiency
explanation: Birds utilize a highly efficient one-way ventilation mechanism. In this system, air flows in a single direction: from the trachea to the posterior air sacs, then through the lungs (where gas exchange occurs), into the anterior air sacs, and is finally expelled. Because of this one-way flow, fresh inhaled air never mixes with stale, used air, maximizing the concentration gradient and gas-exchange efficiency.

questions.q: What is the pathway of air flow in a bird's respiratory system?
opts: Trachea -> Anterior sacs -> Lungs -> Posterior sacs -> Expelled
Trachea -> Posterior sacs -> Lungs -> Anterior sacs -> Expelled
questions.exp: Air in birds flows from the trachea to the posterior sacs, through the lungs, into the anterior sacs, and is then expelled.
